name: @chbrain/khai-composite-artifice
description: khai composite content, the artifice domain: the designed object read whole -- the settlement a made thing strikes among the six design forces (usability, agency, ergonomics, guile, captology, choice-architecture), and whether that settlement serves the user, extracts for the maker, or fails to cohere at all.

khai.tagline: Artifice as composite: the designed object read whole -- the settlement a made thing strikes among the six design forces (usability, agency, ergonomics, guile, captology, choice-architecture), and the drama lives in whether that settlement holds for the user (concord), turns to take from them (extraction), or falls apart against itself (discord) -- with the arrangement the one force no maker can leave unstruck.

card.wire: Attaches at Piece, over six atoms it declares as dependencies -- the first composite to wire engines rather than composites, and the first on the piece type. The root (piece_artifice.md) reads the designed object whole: not any one design force but the settlement a made thing strikes among all six. Usability supplies the honest confirmation, agency the conscription, ergonomics the bodily fit, guile the deception, captology the hook, choice-architecture the arrangement of the options; this composite adds no seventh force but reads what the six make together in one object. Its warrant is the synthesis view of design -- Simon's artifact shaped to serve a goal, Alexander's form as the resolution of forces in a context -- so a piece is never one force but their composition, and the ethics of it lives in whom the composition serves. The sixth force is the one that changes the shape of the question: five of the six can be at zero, and the arrangement cannot, so a maker who strikes nothing has still struck it.
card.issue: Three bridges, the shapes the settlement takes. Concord: the forces aligned for the user -- the object that fits the body, tells the truth of its state, enlists openly or not at all, and arranges its options toward what the user would have chosen knowing everything, neither tricking nor hooking against the one who uses it; Alexander's good fit, the well-made honest tool, and harder than it looks, since abstaining from the arrangement is not on offer. Extraction: the forces aligned for the maker against the user -- the hook and the trick and the coerced enlistment bent to take from the user while wearing the surface of serving them, with the arrangement as the quietest instrument of the take and the one with the best deniability, every setting having an innocent explanation; the attention-economy object, the object designed to extract. Discord: the forces at war with each other -- usable but unfit, honest but hooking, the ergonomics fighting the affordance, and the arrangement inherited from nobody, so no single reading wins and the object misfits itself; Alexander's misfit. A single force alone is an atom's; the composite is the six held in one object and the settlement they reach.
card.require: Two altitudes hold the composite. The law: declared once in the project's Instructions Knowledge chapter, linking the root, so the artifice read runs wherever its atoms are cast. The link, advisory: a piece may link under Load Bearing the bridge it strikes, and the audit surfaces where a play stages a designed object without naming whether its forces hold for the user, extract for the maker, or fall apart.
card.enforce: Structure is checked; coherence is judged. The kit verifies the floor: the law is declared, the composite's own members conform, and every hard link into the atoms resolves through a declared dependency -- here, through the six design engines in turn. Whether a production's object genuinely settles its forces the way the bridge names -- a concord that truly serves, an extraction that truly takes, a discord that truly fails to cohere -- is semantic, taught and reviewed, never failed by the suite. And the six are not equally evidenced: choice-architecture carries its own effect-size caveats in its references, which the composite inherits rather than flattens.
card.setup: Install the composite; its atoms arrive as dependencies -- the six design engines, and through them their own members. Declare the law in the Instructions Knowledge chapter, linking the root. Cast the object's forces from the six engines -- the fit from ergonomics, the confirmation from usability, the enlistment from agency, the trick from guile, the hook from captology, the arrangement of the options from choice-architecture -- then strike the bridge: concord when the forces align for the user, extraction when they align for the maker against the user, discord when they war with each other. Read the object in the settlement it strikes, never in the word artifice alone -- and remember that a made thing that hooks and fits and deceives at once is not three separate findings but one object, and the composite is what reads it as one. Note where the arrangement sits before asking whether it was chosen: the maker who intended nothing by it set it all the same.
